LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.0.label: Spring Water Tune
LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.0.storyText: Qinghe records the water sounds and soft beats after lotus rain has cleared. Reading this volume feels like hearing spring water slip over stone steps while scattered flower shadows sway with the sound.
LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.1.label: Flower Shadow Notes
LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.1.storyText: This manuscript writes of flower shadows, dance steps, and the call-and-response of short melodies. Its sentences are never showy, but they preserve Qinghe's careful observation of the garden plants.
LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.2.label: Listening to Rain
LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.2.storyText: Qinghe breaks the rhythm of rain on lotus leaves into several short scores, then adds performance notes in the margins. The writing is quiet, yet it echoes like fine rain entering the pavilion.
LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.3.label: Lotus Steps
LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.3.storyText: This volume records both dance steps and melody. With a gentle touch, Qinghe sketches sleeves, bell notes, and ripples on the water, giving ordinary performance art a quiet grace.
LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.4.label: Feather Robe by the Lotus
LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.4.storyText: Qinghe writes the water sounds of the Lotus Rain Pavilion as the underlying tone, then notes the light whisper of Neiyu's sleeves at the beginning of a form. The whole volume reads like a brief duet across water.
LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.5.label: Flame Through Rain
LanguageData.MX_Biography_Qinghe.stories.5.storyText: This manuscript sets rainy-night lamplight against the sound of strings. Qinghe turns Zhaoli's words of embers, life-fire, and echoes into turns of melody, adding a bright edge to the pavilion's old tune.
